solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: All four back home

indicators.note: back tells us to read the two pieces from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone announcing that all four members of a family or team have returned home.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or seaside house, so it is a kind of home.

clue.text: Weakness for a dash of vodka on the rocks?

indicators.note: a dash is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of the drink is taken

parts.note: a drink on the rocks is served over ice

explanation.surface: Asking whether a splash of vodka over ice is a forgivable weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a moral failing or bad habit, a weakness of character.

clue.text: Attraction of Philadelphia Freedom live, line after line?

indicators.note: after means coming behind, so one line abbreviation follows the other

parts.note: liberty means freedom
to be means to exist or live

explanation.surface: Elton John's song Philadelphia Freedom performed live, one line after another.
explanation.walkthrough: Philadelphia Freedom is an Elton John hit, which makes the city look like part of a song title rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The cracked bell in Philadelphia is a famous symbol of American independence and a tourist sight.

clue.text: Schedule time to go over gagging order

indicators.note: in a down answer, going over means sitting on top, so this piece comes before the next

parts.note: an age is a period of time
an NDA, a non-disclosure agreement, legally silences someone

explanation.surface: Planning time to review a court order that stops people talking.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a plan or programme for a meeting.

clue.text: R Sunak's predecessor put in prison old people from Europe

indicators.note: put in means one piece is placed inside the other; here the word for prison goes into the former prime minister's name

parts.note: Liz Truss was the UK prime minister before Rishi Sunak
can is slang for a prison

explanation.surface: A political jibe imagining Rishi Sunak's predecessor being jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Etruscans lived in ancient Italy, before Rome absorbed them, which is why they count as old people; 'put in' sets the prison word inside the surname, with Europe's letter in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Etruscans were an ancient civilisation of central Italy, absorbed by Rome.

clue.text: Snoop Dogg's debut in soap ever so funny!

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the rearranged letters
funny means strange, so the letters are rearranged
a debut is a first appearance, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: An excited fan reacting to rapper Snoop Dogg's first appearance in a soap opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snoop' looks like half of the rapper's name, but it is the definition, as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to others' conversation, which is a way to pry.

clue.text: Fight back during bizarre PE lesson

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: Pupils resisting in an odd physical education class.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel attackers is to drive them back or resist them.

clue.text: Second lieutenant eating a grouse: "this meat's spicy"

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the A goes inside these letters

parts.note: beef means a grumble or complaint, as does grouse

explanation.surface: A junior officer complaining about how spicy the meat is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grouse' looks like the game bird, which fits a meat clue, but it is a verb-turned-noun for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt beef is brisket cured in brine with spices, typically served in sandwiches.

clue.text: Caldron occasionally producing hubble-bubble, toil and trouble?

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: The witches' cauldron from Macbeth, chanting 'double, double toil and trouble'.
explanation.walkthrough: The witches in Shakespeare's Macbeth chant over their cauldron; the question mark warns that the phrase is a fanciful definition of fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss and commotion, as in Much Ado About Nothing, which the witches' bustle illustrates.

clue.text: ROFL as Lear goes mad — sudden outburst from star

indicators.note: goes mad means behaves wildly, so the letters are rearranged; it also fits King Lear's madness

explanation.surface: Internet laughter as King Lear loses his mind, like a star's tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: ROFL is internet shorthand for 'rolling on the floor laughing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar flare is a sudden burst of energy from the surface of the Sun, which is a star.

clue.text: On which to watch The Wire?

definitions.text: On which to watch The Wire?

parts.words: On which to watch The Wire?
parts.note: The Wire was an American TV drama, and a wire is also a cable, so the service that delivers programmes by wire is where you would watch it

explanation.surface: A question about where to stream the famous Baltimore crime drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wire is a well-known HBO series; the pun is that television delivered down a wire is exactly what this service is.
explanation.definitionFit: Subscription television delivered through underground cables rather than broadcast through the air.

clue.text: Friend left me in Paris imported cooking fat

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so the French word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: pal is an informal word for a friend
moi is French for me

explanation.surface: A friend has abandoned the speaker in Paris, where cooking fat was brought in from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil pressed from the fruit of the oil palm is widely used as a fat in cooking and processed food.

clue.text: Badly sunburnt, like one in a shell suit?

definitions.text: Badly sunburnt, like one in a shell suit?

parts.words: Badly sunburnt, like one in a shell suit?
parts.note: a shell suit is a shiny nylon tracksuit, but a lobster lives in a shell, and a cooked one is bright red like burnt skin

explanation.surface: A tourist in a cheap nylon tracksuit who has stayed too long in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: A shell suit is a garish 1980s-90s nylon tracksuit; read literally, the creature in a shell is a lobster, whose colour when cooked gives the simile.
explanation.definitionFit: A common idiom for skin turned bright red by the sun, likening it to a boiled crustacean.

clue.text: Classic movie telling van Winkle's story?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1946 film noir starring Humphrey Bogart
second meaning: Rip Van Winkle slept for twenty years, a very long sleep

explanation.walkthrough: Rip Van Winkle, in Washington Irving's tale, sleeps for twenty years in the Catskill Mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The Raymond Chandler film title literally describes a twenty-year nap.

clue.text: American poet, tall chap

parts.note: long means tall or lengthy
a fellow is a man or chap

explanation.surface: Describing a tall man who happens to be an American poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow wrote The Song of Hiawatha and other 19th-century American verse.

clue.text: Old New York Times gem?

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an old copy of the New York Times is a hidden gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York Times' reads as the newspaper, but it splits into NY and X, the times sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Her allies prepared to kick up a fuss

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Her supporters are ready to make trouble on her behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for complaining loudly and causing a disturbance.

clue.text: Gatecrashing international sport's number one set up

parts.note: RU is rugby union, and the 's adds S

indicators.note: in a down answer, set up means raised, so these letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Gatecrashing an international match where the top sportsman was framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' looks like a single idea, but it splits into NO and I, which 'set up' turns into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An intrusion is an unwelcome entry where one is not invited, just as gatecrashing is.

clue.text: Ever more tight, Julius gets stuck into brandy & crème de menthe

indicators.note: gets stuck into means goes inside, so the setter's pronoun is placed within the cocktail

parts.note: a stinger is a cocktail made of brandy and crème de menthe
Julius is the setter, so I

explanation.surface: The setter gets increasingly drunk on cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' looks like drunk, which suits the cocktail, but here it means mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight can mean miserly, so becoming more tight is being stingier with money.

clue.text: Falls to pieces and turns to marijuana

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: takes up pot, a slang word for cannabis

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for deteriorating is read word by word, with pot as slang for marijuana.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to decline into ruin, and literally describes someone taking up cannabis.

clue.text: English playwright denied National Theatre support

indicators.note: denied means refused or deprived of, so the abbreviation is taken away from the name

parts.note: Harold Pinter was an English playwright
NT is the abbreviation for the National Theatre in London

explanation.surface: An English dramatist refused backing by the National Theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a pillar or column bearing the weight of a bridge or arch, a structural support.

clue.text: Plain silly

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both unadorned and, of a person, lacking intelligence or foolish.

clue.text: Comedy producer: dialogue isn't funny son

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a comedy's script is not amusing, son.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing Studios is a London film studio, famous for the 'Ealing comedies' of the 1940s and 50s such as Kind Hearts and Coronets.
explanation.definitionFit: The West London studio produced a celebrated run of postwar British film comedies.

clue.text: Matching piece of bathroom suite advertised on the radio

indicators.note: something on the radio is heard, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: a sink is one item in a matching set of bathroom fittings

explanation.surface: A radio advert for a part of a matching bathroom set.
explanation.walkthrough: A bathroom suite is a matching set of basin, bath and toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: In synch means in time or agreement, so the word can stand for matching up.

clue.text: Support Remain

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a prop or brace
second meaning: to remain in a place

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at backing Remain in the Brexit referendum.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a rope or prop that braces a mast, and to stay is to not leave.

clue.text: Anatoli moved from somewhere further East

indicators.note: moved means shifted about, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Anatoli has relocated from a place further east.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is in Southeast Asia, much further east than Anatoli's Russia, so its people and things are Laotian.

clue.text: Chancellor left out idiot

indicators.note: left out means left is removed, so the abbreviation is taken away from the name

parts.note: Olaf Scholz was the German Chancellor

explanation.surface: Calling a chancellor who was left out of something an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Government cash advance reportedly had a favourable effect

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or heard, so the word is one that sounds like another

parts.note: impressed means made a good impression on someone

explanation.surface: A government advance of money that apparently made a good impression.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprest is a sum advanced from public funds to an official to pay expenses.

clue.text: Wife after getting drunk with husband at home is very delicate

indicators.note: drunk suggests being thrown about unsteadily, so this word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A wife who drinks with her husband at home turns out to be very fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting drunk' looks like part of the story about the wife, but it only signals that the letters of 'after' are scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin like a wafer biscuit, so extremely slight or flimsy.

clue.text: Vacant English politician, gutless Tory

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: gutless means without insides, so only the outer letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: A cowardly, empty-headed English Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something with nothing in it, such as an unoccupied room.
